div.p: The development of avionics systems has promoted the introduction of the time-triggered concept. The Time-triggered Ethernet (TTE) is a deterministic, synchronous, conflict-free network protocol based on the IEEE 802.3 Ethernet standards and is compatible with ARINC 664p7 protocol. It supports real-time application of mixed-criticality by providing three types of traffic: time-triggered (TT) traffic, which has low jitter and bounded end-to-end delay; rate-constrained (RC) traffic, which has bounded end-to-end delay; and best-effort (BE) traffic, which cannot ensure end-to-end delay. Carrying out offline routing and scheduling configuration on TT traffic ensures the conflict-free of TT traffic in the transmission link. Since the priority of TT traffic is higher than that of RC traffic, ignoring RC traffic in the process of configuring TT traffic routing may make the RC traffic transmission delay very large, exceeding the scope of network design requirements. The issue of concern in this paper is the routing configuration for TT traffic and RC traffic in the TTE network. Under the premise of ensuring the schedulability of TT traffic, the transmission path of TT and RC traffic is configured and optimized, and the end-to-end delay of RC traffic is reduced. Through the network topology information and network traffic information, a load balancing strategy based on the genetic algorithm is used in this paper to configure TT traffic routing, and a path cost strategy is used to configure RC traffic routing. Experimental results from multiple use cases show that routing configuration for TT traffic has a great effect on the end-to-end delay of RC traffic.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: The Ethernet [1] is a low-cost and high-speed network, but in time-critical, strictly deterministic, or security-critical situations, the Ethernet lacks relevant guarantee mechanisms. Avionics Full Duplex Switched Ethernet (AFDX) [2] is a network based on the ARINC 664p7 protocol. It provides deterministic timing for real-time application through the concept of virtual links (VLs) and the concept of rate-constrained (RC) traffic on the basis of extending the Ethernet. Unlike integrated networks that use event-triggered communication, such as Ethernet and AFDX, the time-triggered (TT) communication of the Time-triggered Ethernet (TTE) network [3] [4] has strict deterministic timing and traffic isolation based on time windows to avoid the end-to-end jitter caused by event-triggered queuing of multiplexed. The TTE network provides three different traffic grades: TT traffic, RC traffic, and best-effort (BE) traffic. TT traffic is used in applications with strict delay, delay jitter, and deterministic requirements. All TT traffic is transmitted on the network at predefined time windows and has priority over other traffic types. In such a situation, when an end system does not use the time slot assigned to TT traffic, the remaining bandwidth can be provided for the use of other traffic types. RC traffic is used in applications with less strict degree of determinism and real-time requirements. RC traffic ensures that there is a predefined bandwidth for each application. Unlike TT traffic, the transmission of RC traffic does not follow the system-wide synchronous time benchmark, and different communication controllers may transmit frames to the same receiver at the same moment. Therefore, RC traffic may be in queue at the switches, leading to an increase in the transmission delay jitter. Because the transmission rate of RC traffic is constrained in an a priori manner within a certain limit and controlled by the network switch, the upper limit of transmission delay jitter can be calculated offline, and the loss of frames can be avoided. BE traffic realizes the traditional ethernet communication method. The delay is not ensured, BE traffic are applicable to the remaining bandwidth of the network, and its priority is lower than those of TT and RC traffic.

The concern of this paper is the routing configuration for TT traffic and RC traffic. In terms of traffic routing configuration, many works have already been performed. AFDX network routing configuration based on the trajectory approach [5] can make the maximum end-to-end delay of all the VLs to be smaller than the system requirements. An integer linear programming (ILP) method [6] is used to solve the routing problem of several thousand VLs, and its purpose is to reduce bandwidth consumption, thereby obtaining greater flexibility when adding new VLs or modifying existing VLs. In POGA algorithm [7], the real-time performance of RC traffic in the network is used as the optimization goal, and the network load balancing is considered at the same time. The load balancing routing strategy and the minimum hop routing strategy are two commonly used strategies for solving network routing problems. The aim of the load balancing routing strategy is to select routing that balances the link traffic, and a traffic balancing routing algorithm in the Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS) network is proposed in [8] and [9]. The minimum hop routing strategy considers finding the routing in the network with the least number of hops from the source to the destination, and an improved minimum hop routing algorithm in the Quality of Service (QoS)-constrained network is proposed in [10]. Unlike the AFDX network, the TTE network has high-priority TT traffic, and the routing configuration of the TT traffic will have a great impact on the RC traffic. Therefore, the TT routing in the network plays a key role in the overall performance of the network.

The structure of the paper is as follows: Section 2 is an introduction of the TTE network interconnection configuration, Section 3 is a description of the problem in this paper, Section 4 is a specific introduction of our method, Section 5 is the experimental results, and Section 6 is the conclusion of this paper.

div.head: II. TTE NETWORK INTERCONNECTION CONFIGURATION
div.p: A. Switching architecture of TTE network 1. Star-shaped switching architecture According to the characteristics of the switching network, a small-scale TTE network can be interconnected by using a star-shaped architecture, as shown in Fig. 1. The advantages of the star-shaped architecture are as follows:
(1) Simple to control. Any node is only connected to the central node. It is easy to monitor and manage the network.

(2) Easy to diagnose and isolate faults. The central node to the connection line can be isolated one by one to carry out fault detection and location. A fault in a single connection point only affects one piece of equipment and does not affect the entire network.
(3) Convenient to service. The central node can conveniently provide service and network reconfiguration to each node.
Disadvantages of the star-shaped architecture are as follows:
(1) The single-topology architecture is unsuitable for a network with many nodes and high throughput.
(2) The burden on the central node is heavy, which forms a "bottleneck". Once a fault occurs in the central node, then the whole network is affected.

2. Extended star-shaped switching architecture According to the characteristics of the switching network, a large-scale TTE network can be interconnected by using an extended star-shaped architecture, as shown in Fig. 2. The extended star-shaped architecture has the advantages of the star-shaped architecture and supports a network with more nodes and greater throughput. The disadvantages of the extended star-shaped architecture are as follows:

div.head: ES SW
div.p: (1) If the partitioned areas of the terminal end systems are unreasonable, the traffic of cross-area will increase. The increased traffic will exacerbate the burden on the central node and seriously affect the network performance.
(2) If fault appears in the central point, most of the components of the network will be disconnected.

3. Mesh-star mixed architecture A network with high reliability requirements that when a switch is in failure, the other network parts cannot be completely paralyzed and can still continue to work. Neither the star-shaped architecture nor the extended star-shaped architecture can satisfy this requirement. In these two kinds of networks, the working state of some key switches determines the communication state of the entire network. Therefore, a mesh-star mixed architecture interconnection configuration is proposed, as shown in Fig. 3. The star-shaped architecture is between the switch and the terminal end system, and the mesh architecture is between the switches. In this way, the advantages of the star-shaped architecture and the mesh architecture are combined to guarantee the reliability requirements of the network. The advantages of the mesh-star mixed architecture configuration are as follows:

(1) The network has high reliability. There are two or more than two communication paths between any two node switches in the communication subnetwork. In this way, when fault occurs in a path, the frames can still be sent to the switch through another path.
(2) The network can be set up in various shapes using multiple communication channels and multiple transmission rates.
(3) It is easy for the nodes within the network to share resources. Fig. 3. Mesh-star mixed architecture of TTE network (4) The traffic distribution for the frames along the links can be improved.
(5) The best path can be selected, and the transmission delay is small.

div.head: B. Redundant network architecture of TTE network
div.p: 1. Single-network architecture Single-network architecture refers to an entire system that uses one set of networks to carry out the transmission of communication tasks, as shown in Fig. 4. In an application situation in which the reliability requirement is not high, the TTE network can use a single network to carry out the transmission of communication tasks. The single network can use different switching architectures according to different network scales and different design requirements.
Compared with the dual-redundancy network, the advantages of the single-network architecture are as follows:
(1) The network has simple transceiving devices-the transmitting end system needs to maintain only one transmitting device, and the receiving end system maintains one receiving device.
(2) The network has a comparatively simple receiving mechanism without need for a redundant receiving strategy, and there is no redundant judgment error.
The disadvantages of the single-network architecture are as follows:
(1) The network has low reliability. If a network fails, then the entire communication system fails.
(2) The network has low communication efficiency. The loss of a data packet will affect the communication process related to that data packet.

div.head: Dual-redundancy network architecture
div.p: The dual-redundancy network refers to two sets of networks that carry the communication tasks of the entire communication system. The transmission objects of the two sets of networks are completely identical, but there is no intersection between the equipment of the two sets of networks, and there is no association at all between the two sets for the same communication tasks. In certain situations, such as in an avionics system, the communication network is required to have high reliability and communication efficiency, but the single network cannot satisfy the system design requirements. The dual-redundancy network is able to quickly increase the reliability and communication efficiency of the entire communication system under the premise of not substantially changing the entire system design. Therefore, in situations in which reliability is critical, the dual-redundancy network has a very high application value.
Compared with the single network, the advantages of the dual-redundancy network architecture are as follows:
(1) The network has high reliability-if one network fails, then the other network becomes the communication network in order to guarantee that the entire communication system can continue to run.

(2) The network has high communication efficiency-if a data packet is lost, then high-efficiency communication between processes is guaranteed by the reception of that data packet on the other network.
The disadvantages of the dual-redundancy network architecture are as follows:

(1) Two sets of transceiving devices are needed. The transmitting end system needs to maintain two transmission devices, and when a data packet is transmitted, the data packet not only is sent into the first network but also has to be copied into the other network.
(2) The receiving mechanism is complex, a redundant receiving strategy must be designed, and there are some situations in which the redundant judgment is wrong.

In accordance with whether or not the interconnection configurations of the two sets of networks are completely the same, the dual-redundancy network can be divided into a symmetric dual-redundancy network and an asymmetric dualredundancy network. A symmetric dual-redundancy network is shown in Fig. 5, and the interconnection architectures of the two sets of networks are completely consistent. An asymmetric dual-redundancy network is shown in Fig. 6, and the two sets In the symmetric dual-redundancy network, if the two sets of networks use the same routing strategy to configure the communication tasks, the same communication tasks will reach the receiving end system at almost the same time, which is conducive to the determination of the redundant receiving strategy; if different routing strategies are used to configure the communication tasks, then there will be a certain difference in the time at which the same communication tasks reach the receiving end system, which is not conducive to the determination of the redundant receiving strategy.

There is no consideration for the routing strategy and the spatial layout of the switching equipment in an asymmetric dual-redundancy network. Compared with a symmetric dualredundancy network, the disadvantage of an asymmetric dualredundancy network is that regardless of what kind of routing strategy is used, there is a certain difference in the time at which the same communication tasks reach the receiving end system, which is not conducive to the determination of the redundant receiving strategy; the advantage is that spatial layout can be freely designed.

Three end system systems and one switch are included in this example. We used an undirected graph G (V, E) to model the TTE network, wherein V = ES SW represents the set of terminal end systems and switches and E is the set of physical links. div.p: Equation ( 1) is used to evaluate the schedulability of the TT traffic f T T i . u T T i is formed by the accumulation of two parts; the first item represents the bandwidth needed for transmission on the link for the traffic f T T i , and the second item represents the bandwidth consumed by the interference of the remaining traffic other than traffic f T T i with the traffic f T T i on the link . div.head: IV. PATH OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHM
div.p: The genetic algorithm (GA) used in this paper is a heuristic algorithm that gives a high-quality feasible solution that can satisfy the network performance for each actual example and it can solve the combination optimization problem at an acceptable cost (referring to computing time and space).

The routing strategy in this paper uses GA based on K shortest paths (KSP) [14]. The inputs are the network topology architecture G (V, E) and a set of TT traffic and RC traffic F = F T T ∪ F RC . Through several iterations, a routing set R with TT traffic that has load balancing performance and RC traffic that has path cost balancing is output. The algorithm terminates at a given time limit or there is no improvement in the value of the objective function after a given number of iterations.

The TTE network path optimization algorithm is as shown in Algorithm 1. Quantitative analysis of the effect of the frames on the links helps to find a set of load-balanced TT traffic routing. Equation ( 2) represents the load of all the TT data frames transmitted on the link.

The routing strategy is the minimization of the objective function OBJ(T T ), and the value of the objective function is nonnegative. Therefore, the objective function can be directly used as a fitness function. The GA is composed of four steps-the evaluation, selection, crossover, and mutation (Line 9) of the individual fitness. The selection step in the GA is the selection of an individual from the parent population to go to the next population in accordance with the individual fitness function. In this paper, the roulette wheel selection method is used to choose the individual from the parent population. By carrying out crossover and mutation on the selected individual, we can obtain a new population of size N. The algorithm terminates at the given number of iterations or at the given time limit, and then we obtain a set of optimized TT traffic paths R T T .

Therefore, the objective function OBJ(RC) of the RC traffic routing optimization can be obtained.
div.formula: OBJ(RC) = α • Cost RC LB f RC i + (1 -α) • Cost RC M H f RC i(7)
div.p: α = 1 means that the objective function uses a load balancing strategy; α = 0 means that the objective function uses the shortest path strategy. The shortest path strategy selects the routing with the smallest number of hops, which improves the resource utilization rate, thereby making the mean value of the link utilization rate comparatively small, but it cannot limit the variance of the link utilization rate. A local obstruction situation may appear in the network, leading to a sharp increase in end-to-end delay in passing through RC traffic. The load balancing strategy balances the utilization rates of all the links, which makes the variance of the link utilization rate comparatively small and holds back the local obstruction, but tortuous routing may be selected due to this. An increase in the number of hops reduces the resource utilization rate, and the mean value of the link utilization rate becomes larger, leading to a certain degree of increase in the end-to-end delay for all the RC traffic in the network. In this paper, α = 0.5 is set to combine the advantages of the two strategies.

K f RC,j i represents the j-th shortest path corresponding to traffic f RC i . By randomly selecting the number of the traffic f RC i , we can generate the initial total population of the GA algorithm (Line 16). The routing strategy is the minimization of the objective function OBJ(RC), and the value of the objective function is nonnegative. Therefore, the objective function can be directly used as a fitness function. The iterations stop after the algorithm satisfies the termination conditions, and a set of optimized RC traffic paths R RC is obtained. Finally, the algorithm outputs the set of TTE network traffic optimization paths R = R T T ∪ R RC .

div.head: V. EXPERIMENTAL EVALUATION
div.p: To assess and verify the accuracy and scalability of our method, we used the network topology shown in Fig. 8. The TC1 use case is configured with 50 TT flows and 50 RC flows. The value range for the traffic period is 1-128 ms, and the range for the frame length is 64-1518 bytes. The link rate of this network is 100 Mbit/s. The TT traffic and RC traffic routing is configured through the routing optimization algorithm, and the SMT algorithm is used to generate the TT traffic offline time schedule table. The SPA and the random path algorithm (RPA) are compared with this method. The RC traffic delay with the three methods are shown in Fig. 9. The worst-case end-to-end delay of the RC traffic is the smallest by using the load balancing algorithm (GPA). The average is 7.96% smaller than that of the RPA and 6.41% smaller than that of the SPA. Fig. 10 shows the average deviation of RC traffic delay of each node port in the network. It can be seen that there is a big difference between the delay and the average value at the node port [SW 7 , SW 4 ] (Port No. 19). This method can effectively improve the congestion of the node port. Compared with RPA and SPA, the average delay of node port in this method is reduced by 3.73% and 2.54% respectively. And the standard deviation is reduced from 332.39us and 336.53us to 289.34us, which effectively balances the port load of each node.

TC2 is configured with 50 TT flows and 80 RC flows, wherein the TT traffic configuration parameters and schedule table are consistent with those in the TC1 use case. The RC traffic delay results with the three methods are as shown in Fig. 11. The worst-case end-to-end delay of the RC traffic is the smallest by using GPA. The average is 5.54% smaller than that of the RPA and 4.28% smaller than that of the SPA.

Therefore, the routing optimization strategy for the network traffic can effectively reduce the delay in the RC traffic. When the RC traffic load increases, the profitability obtained by the method in this paper decreases. The development of avionics systems has promoted the introduction of the time-triggered concept. The TTE network supports real-time application of mixed security by providing three types of traffic: TT traffic, which has low jitter and bounded end-to-end delay; RC traffic, which has bounded end-to-end delay; and BE traffic, which cannot ensure end-toend delay. Carrying out offline routing configuration on TT traffic ensures the conflict-free nature of TT traffic on the transmission link. Since the priority of TT traffic is higher than that of RC traffic, ignoring RC traffic in the process of configuring TT traffic routing may make the RC traffic transmission delay too big. Carrying out routing optimization on the TT traffic and RC traffic can effectively reduce the worst-case end-to-end delay of the RC traffic. Additionally, the average delay at each node port in the network will decrease, and there will not be a situation in which several ports are jammed. In this paper, the load balancing strategy based on the GA is used to configure the TT traffic routing, and the path cost strategy is used to configure the RC traffic routing. Experimental data show that path configuration for the TT traffic can effectively reduce the end-to-end delay of the RC traffic.
